source_name: AmCham North Macedonia — Members List
why_relevant: Over 130 member organisations across five tiers (Patron, Corporate, Business, Entrepreneur, NGO), including major foreign investors and banks. Tier is itself a proxy for institutional weight, and the roster enumerates foreign-owned financial actors that other cells must monitor.

source_name: Foreign Investors Council North Macedonia (Совет на странски инвеститори)
why_relevant: Represents roughly 40 foreign-capital companies including foreign bank subsidiaries; Viktor Mizo is reported as President. FIC runs quarterly meetings with the Prime Minister and the government economic team, and its assembly elects a board — both membership and board composition map foreign institutional weight in MK finance.

source_name: Асоцијација на финансиски друштва на Северна Македонија (AFD)
why_relevant: Self-describes as uniting fintech and other non-bank financial-services providers; formed with a constitutive session on 27 June 2019 electing a Management Board drawn from different financial activities. Its site publishes member-accession posts (e.g. Kredi Yes joining in April 2021), which are direct organisation-change events, and it co-organises sector initiatives with the Insurance Supervision Agency (InsurHack Skopje).

source_name: Стопанска комора на северо-западна Македонија / Oda Ekonomike e Maqedonisë Veriperëndimore (OEMVP)
why_relevant: The second major general chamber in MK, operating in Albanian and Macedonian, with its own elected leadership and member base. Necessary to avoid an Albanian-language blind spot in the actor map — several MK banks and financial companies have Albanian-language business communities that the Skopje chamber under-represents.

source_name: Германо-Македонска стопанска комора (AHK Nordmazedonien)
why_relevant: Bilateral chamber (German AHK network) with its own member roster and board; German-owned or German-serving financial and IT firms in MK appear here. AHK chambers typically publish a member directory and an elected board, and their event programmes reveal which executives currently front the payments/finance agenda.

source_name: Сојуз на стопански комори на Македонија (Macedonian Chambers of Commerce)
source_subtype: chamber social presence (proxy for main site)
why_relevant: A third chamber body (chamber.mk) distinct from mchamber.mk and OEMVP; its sections and elected officers add another slice of the business-association map. Only an active social presence was confirmed in this pass, so the social page is offered as the entry point to reach the organisation's current web home.

source_name: Fintech.mk / FintechMK community
why_relevant: Described as the first fintech community in Macedonia, initiated by fintech practitioners. It is not a formal association with elected governance, but its events and organiser names reveal who the active fintech operators and evangelists are — useful for enumerating early-stage payments actors that no chamber directory captures. Note: no independent .mk association website was confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Bankometar.mk — chamber and association event coverage
why_relevant: Specialist MK banking-news outlet that reports association and chamber events in detail, including NBRM workshops hosted at the Chamber on practical SEPA payment aspects and the first Fintech Academy. Acts as a secondary confirmation layer and often names the individual bank/chamber officials present when the institutions themselves publish only a bare announcement.

source_name: Biznis Vesti — association leadership reporting
why_relevant: Business outlet that reports association elections as standalone news — e.g. the announcement that Kosta Mitrovski became the new president of the Macedonian Banking Association for a four-year term. Provides date-stamped confirmation and mandate length that the association's own static pages omit.

source_name: Invest North Macedonia — Useful links (business associations index)
why_relevant: Government investment-agency curated index of chambers, associations and business bodies — a low-cost way to discover association bodies missed by keyword search, and semi-authoritative on which associations the state recognises as counterparties.

source_name: US Commercial Service — North Macedonia Principal Business Associations
why_relevant: An externally compiled enumeration of the principal MK business associations with contact details — valuable as a cross-check that the association universe assembled from local search is complete, and as a historical snapshot. Hosted on a legacy/archived US government domain, so treat currency as low.

source_name: LinkedIn organisation pages for MK associations and chambers
why_relevant: Associations post board-election announcements, new-member welcomes and secretariat hires to LinkedIn faster and in more personal detail than to their websites; FIC's page was observed posting member-executive features. Also the only practical way to observe secretariat staff churn, which no association publishes formally.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (e-nabavki.gov.mk) Public Access portal
why_relevant: Single national tender portal. Every contracting authority (договорен орган) must publish notices, tender dossiers, award decisions and 'известување за склучен договор' here. Notices for банкарски услуги, платен промет, ПОС терминали, е-плаќање and core-system consultancy carry the buying unit's contact officer, the winning economic operator and often the key-expert/CV requirements — a direct read on who staffs payments programmes on the public route and a master pointer to the supplier population.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Склучени / Реализирани договори (concluded and realised contracts grid)
why_relevant: Institution-by-institution grid of concluded and realised contracts with supplier name and value. This is the award-side view: which vendor won a bank/POS/e-payment contract for which public buyer, and therefore which supplier is about to staff or expand a delivery team.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (Public Procurement Bureau, BJN) — bjn.gov.mk
why_relevant: Regulator/operator of the ESJN. Publishes rulebooks, ESJN user manuals, annual public-procurement reports and news (e.g. announcement that concluded contracts are published on ESJN). Its guidance defines what fields award notices must contain — essential for building a reliable extraction schema — and its reports name market structure and top suppliers.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Биро за јавни набавки / Е-јавни набавки institutional pages
why_relevant: Ministry-of-Finance side of the procurement machinery; also links the ministry's own tender notices. MoF is the buyer for treasury/payment-system related consultancy and for the state's banking arrangements.

source_name: Трезор — Treasury Department, Ministry of Finance
why_relevant: The Treasury runs the single treasury account, the register of budget users and all денарски/девизни payment execution for the public sector. Organisational notices, treasury-operations instructions (Упатство за начинот на трезорско работење) and reform announcements reveal who owns public payment rails and when a payment-system change is coming that will need vendors and staff.

source_name: Open Finance портал (open.finance.gov.mk) — public spending transactions
why_relevant: Transaction-level publication of budget-user spending. Payments to named suppliers for banking/POS/IT services corroborate ESJN awards and expose contracts that never surfaced as a visible tender, plus ongoing consultancy burn rates.

source_name: Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (DKZJN) — appeals decisions
why_relevant: Publishes complaints received daily and the decisions taken at sessions. Appeal files in banking/POS/IT tenders name the bidders, the disputed technical/staffing criteria (often key-expert qualification requirements) and the contracting authority's officials — an unusually rich, named view of the supplier and expert population that award notices summarise only briefly.

source_name: Државен завод за ревизија (State Audit Office, DZR) — audit reports on institutions
why_relevant: Regularity/performance audits of the National Bank, DKZJN, ministries and public enterprises routinely detail procurement of banking and IT services, contract values, and internal organisational units — a retrospective but highly reliable read on who buys payments capability and how the buying unit is structured.

source_name: Народна банка на РСМ — Јавни набавки (central bank procurement)
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and the operator/overseer of national payment systems (MIPS, oversight of KIBS). Its tenders for payment-system software, HSM/card infrastructure and consultancy are the closest public-route proxy for core payments programme staffing at the top of the sector.

source_name: Царинска управа на РСМ — Јавни набавки (Customs Administration tender dossiers)
why_relevant: Customs publishes full tender dossiers (тендерска документација) as PDFs, including service procurements. A confirmed live PDF path exists (tenderskaOp162017.pdf). Dossiers state required expert profiles and the contracting authority's contact person — exactly the named-role signal the cell targets. Customs is also a heavy user of card/e-payment collection.

source_name: Ministry-level and agency procurement pages (МВР, МО, МТСП, Министерство за економија и труд, Влада)
why_relevant: Each contracting authority mirrors its own notices with local contact officers and, often, richer dossiers than the ESJN summary. Collectively they are the buyer-side population for payment-acceptance and core-system procurement, and the pages name the responsible procurement unit.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU)
why_relevant: Publishes EU-funded and above-threshold notices naming North Macedonia, including IPA technical-assistance service contracts. TA contract notices and awards list the winning consortium and, in the ToR, the key-expert positions (team leader, senior/junior experts) with required profiles — the most explicit public statement of who is being staffed onto a payments/PFM programme.

source_name: DG NEAR / Enlargement — IPA financial assistance to North Macedonia (programming and action documents)
why_relevant: Action documents and Commission Implementing Decisions describe upcoming PFM/financial-sector/digitalisation interventions before any tender exists — a leading indicator of which programmes will need contractors and experts, and which national institution will host them. Also names EBRD/EIB-channelled financial-sector facilities.

source_name: EEAS — Delegation of the EU to North Macedonia (calls for tenders / vacancies)
why_relevant: The Delegation is the contracting authority for many IPA service contracts and publishes local calls, contract awards and project-team announcements not always visible in TED search defaults.
